outcomes.original: Filing step: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State, obtain an EIN from the IRS, and register the business with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector. What to say: File LLC Articles of Organization (Form LLC-1, $70) or corporation articles ($100) online at the CA Secretary of State. The same day, apply for an EIN at irs.gov (free, issued immediately). Within 30 days, register the business with SF Treasurer & Tax Collector for a Business Registration Certificate ($55–$700 based on gross receipts). The Business Account Number (BAN) from the city registration is required for every other city permit, so do this step early. If the business name differs from the legal entity name, file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk and publish it in a newspaper within 45 days.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for a California Seller's Permit online with the CDTFA and arrange workers' compensation insurance. What to say: The seller's permit is free and often issued the same day when you register online at cdtfa.ca.gov. ABC will not issue an alcohol license until the seller's permit exists, so get it before applying to ABC. Register as an employer with CA EDD within 15 days of hiring (free, online, 1–7 days). Arrange workers' compensation insurance with a licensed carrier or the State Fund (mandatory from the first employee); several city permits ask for proof of coverage.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Have at least one owner or employee complete a Certified Food Protection Manager exam and have all food-handling employees obtain California Food Handler Cards. What to say: At least one person must pass an ANSI-accredited food safety certification exam (ServSafe, Prometric, etc., $100–$250, valid 5 years) within 60 days of opening; the health inspector will ask for the certificate at the pre-opening inspection. Every employee who handles food must obtain a Food Handler Card ($7–$15, online course takes ~2 hours, valid 3 years) within 30 days of hire. If the business will serve alcohol, every alcohol server and their managers must complete RBS (Responsible Beverage Service) training ($3 registration + $10–$25 course) within 60 days of hire; keep the certification list on site for ABC inspections.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If tenant improvements or kitchen work are planned, or if no kitchen or grease interceptor exists, file a building permit application with DBI and route it to DPH for plan check. What to say: The description states no tenant improvements are planned, but if the space does not already have a commercial kitchen, hood, hand sinks, and grease interceptor that meet code, those installations will trigger a building permit and DPH plan check. Submit two sets of scaled plans, equipment layout, and menu to DPH via their online portal. DPH will route the building permit application to Planning for zoning sign-off. Schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% complete and a final inspection at least two weeks before opening. If no kitchen work is needed, skip this step.
outcomes.note: The cited FOG program record does not describe DPH plan check procedures, submission requirements to DPH, routing to Planning, or inspection scheduling.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for a Health Permit to Operate online with DPH at least one month before opening, and schedule the pre-opening inspection. What to say: Apply online at sfdph.org/ehsBizPortal with your BAN, Location ID (LIN), and federal tax ID. The $470 Permit to Operate application includes the initial inspection; the annual license fee for restaurants is $0 for FY2026–28. DPH will inspect to confirm the facility matches the approved plans, all equipment is in place, and a certified food safety manager is on staff. Schedule the inspection at least two weeks in advance. Common failures (missing hand sinks, unsealed surfaces, no hot water) push openings by 2–3 weeks, so walk the space against the DPH checklist before calling for the inspection.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If beer-and-wine only (Type 41): apply to ABC for a Type 41 license online, post the public notice at the premises for 30 days, and submit the Planning and Police referral responses to ABC. What to say: File the ABC-257 application online at abc.ca.gov with the signed lease, seller's permit, entity documents, and filing fee. ABC will mail you a notice to post at the premises for 30 days. Simultaneously, ABC will send referrals to SFPD and Planning; Planning's zoning sign-off for a Type 41 at a bona fide eating place in the NCD-Lower Polk Street district has been approved in 2–21 days in comparable cases. If no one protests during the 30-day posting and the census tract is not undue-concentration, expect ABC to issue the license in roughly 60–120 days from application. If the tract is high-crime or undue-concentration, ABC may require a Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN) letter from the city, adding time; confirm the tract status with ABC or SFPD before applying.
outcomes.note: Records show only Planning referral decisions and timelines; ABC procedures, forms, posting requirements, and issuance timelines are not stated in these records.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 14 to 45 days. Estimated government cost: $470 to $1,000. Notes: This range is the time and government cost to obtain a health permit to operate, the only approval the rules classified as allowed (no discretionary hearing required). The health permit is issued 14–45 days after application once the pre-opening inspection confirms the facility is ready, per the catalog entry. The $470–$1,000 range is the DPH Permit to Operate application fee including the initial inspection; the FY2026–27 annual license fee for restaurants is $0. This is a time to approval, not to denial or withdrawal. It does not include the ABC license, because the rules could not decide which ABC license type applies (the description does not state what alcohol will be served or how the license will be obtained). The building permit and change-of-use timeline is also excluded because the rules could not establish whether one is needed (the records do not show what the space was last used as, and the existing occupancy group is not in public records). The zoning and use row is insufficient information (formula retail not ruled out), so no discretionary hearing timeline is included here. State and federal business formation (EIN, entity registration, seller's permit, employer registration, insurance, food safety certifications, RBS training) add roughly 1–14 days and can be completed in parallel with city permits. Sign permit for exterior signage adds 7–45 days if new signage is installed. Music licenses (ASCAP, BMI) for recorded music add 1–7 days and should be set up in the final two weeks before opening. All day and cost figures are from the catalog entries cited.
